With South Carolina’s Education Scholarship Trust Fund, parents can customize their kids’ education. There are similar programs in 16 other states. This isn’t a loophole—it’s the program working as designed, says Cato’s @ColleenHroncich. 
ow.ly/ZeoO50YEA63

Trump’s Maritime Action Plan aims to revive US shipbuilding with subsidies and mandates. But US-built ships cost about 5x global prices, and shipyards face labor and supply chain shortages exacerbated by US immigration restrictions and tariffs. 

Protectionism won’t make them competitive—or fix naval shipbuilding, says Cato’s @cpgrabow. 
ow.ly/eYoM50YEzIh

The answer to Washington’s affordability crisis isn’t more government intervention—it's less. The better path is sound money and more economic freedom to supply everything from housing and childcare to energy and food.

Video

Hungary has been a “laboratory” for illiberal nationalism under Viktor Orbán, Cato’s @johanknorberg explains. After 16 years: weaker checks and balances, a steep press-freedom slide, and a poorer, less free country—hardly the promised model. 

Learn more: 
ow.ly/jen750YGGFg

FCC Chairman Carr's pressure on CNN—whatever you think of their war reporting—is the latest alarming example of government officials trying to shape news coverage, says Cato’s @bskorup. The real fix: strip the FCC of the vague authority that makes these threats possible. 

ow.ly/Qfa550YGKUT

Trump's new "simplified" metal tariffs actually raise costs for most importers. A lower rate on a much bigger tax base means higher duties — it's a tariff hike dressed up as reform, says Cato’s @clark_packard.

ow.ly/3E5Q50YFOnq

A federal judge just tossed Elon Musk’s lawsuit against advertisers who departed X, ruling that the companies' actions did not violate antitrust law. The wider issue is when government legal pressure against ad boycotts crosses the line into violating free speech, says Walter Olson.   
ow.ly/XCfx50YGIgs

Now is the moment to have a real conversation about tariffs—and for Congress to reclaim its authority, says @RepJimmyPanetta at a Cato Institute event. 
  
Watch the full event here: ow.ly/6n6K50YFX7A

Video

DOJ prosecutors wield immense power—but a new DOJ rule would let the US Attorney General review ethics complaints first, delaying or sidelining independent state bar investigations. That undercuts Congress’s intent that federal lawyers face the same standards as everyone else, says Cato’s @foxmike90.   
ow.ly/qQYq50YGI4k

Vice President JD Vance visited Hungary to champion PM Viktor Orbán as a defender of Western civilization. Cato's @MrRBourne talks with @johanknorberg about Orbán's real record: eroded checks and balances, crony capitalism, and social policies that fell short of his ambitions.

Apple: ow.ly/eH8a50YGGNo
Spotify: ow.ly/gh9y50YGGNp
Our website: ow.ly/bPNH50YGGNn

Trump called April 2, 2025, “Liberation Day” for US manufacturing. One year later: factories didn’t come back, jobs fell, and tariffs mostly raised costs for Americans. Production shifted to places like Vietnam—not the US, reports Cato’s @clark_packard. 
ow.ly/vxWo50YGGMM

The Main Street Act would cut red tape for small banks, make oversight more objective, and limit government pressure on banks to drop customers. It gets a lot right, but it could expand regulator discretion—the problem the bill is trying to solve, explain Cato’s @norbertjmichel and @ChristianJKruse.

ow.ly/O1ck50YFG6l

Free expression is now met with growing suspicion across the globe. In “The Future of Free Speech,” @JMchangama and Jeff Kosseff discuss how we got here. Join us for a live conversation. nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1rxmqoldZ…

CBDCs are being sold as a fix for everything—but they can’t do it all. Many promises conflict, and in reality they’d mostly duplicate existing services or expand government control. If there’s no clear problem to solve, why build one? Says Cato’s @EconWithNick. ow.ly/nG2650YE5vC

Muslim immigrants in the United States are integrating and adopting mainstream views over time even more than polls of Muslims indicate, reports Cato’s @David_J_Bier. 
ow.ly/fC1u50YEzog

Banning data centers is like banning railroads at the start of the industrial age, say Cato’s @jrhuddles and Christopher Gardner. Instead of blocking AI infrastructure, states should consider forward-looking policies, so innovation and consumers both have the infrastructure and energy resources they need.

ow.ly/ja0550YFGHA

The US has taken military action against Iran—but Congress hasn’t declared war.
  
The Founders and the Constitution are clear: war making belongs to Congress, not the executive branch, says Cato’s @katherinet57.
  
In this video, she explains the War Powers Act and why no war should be fought without our consent.

Video

The problem in jury selection isn’t just racial bias—it’s jury stacking. Prosecutors exclude jurors who are skeptical of the government or open to acquittal, often using race as a proxy. Banning racial discrimination alone won’t fix that, says Cato’s Matthew Cavedon.
ow.ly/g1WE50YE5u6

A $100,000 fee on H-1B visas is basically a tariff on talent—and it’s backfiring. Rural health care, scientific research, and other U.S. industries are struggling to fill open positions, while large corporations are moving jobs abroad. The result is less innovation and a weaker economy—the opposite of what was promised, explains Cato’s @scottlincicome.

ow.ly/cNTK50YF40u

Trump's FY2027 budget hikes defense spending 42% while ignoring the entitlement programs driving the debt. Shuffling dollars from domestic programs to the Pentagon won't fix a $2 trillion deficit either. Congress needs to cut spending, not redirect it, argues Cato’s @LettDominik.

ow.ly/pPvV50YEGzq
